The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are two ways to create a Compute‑Engine VM that has a **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you run | Where you run it |
|--------|--------------|------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (after `gcloud init` and `gcloud auth login`) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, your own script) |

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Pick a project, zone and machine type
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # or any zone that supports GPUs
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed

# 2️⃣  Name of the instance
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 3️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata=serial-port-enable=TRUE \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --network-interface=network=default,subnet=default \
  --service-account=$(gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter="displayName:default" --format="value(email)") \
  --description="Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with RTX A6000 GPU"
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | 100 GB SSD boot disk (adjust if you need more) |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | VM will be migrated during maintenance windows |
| `--scopes` | Gives the VM full Cloud‑Platform access (needed for GPU drivers) |
| `--tags` | Opens ports 80/443 if you want a web server |
| `--service-account` | Uses the default Compute Engine service account (or specify another) |

> **Tip:**  
> *If you need a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-8` or `n1-highcpu-8`), just change `--machine-type`.  
> *If you want a pre‑emptible VM, add `--preemptible`.*

---

## 2. REST API (curl example)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)   # or use a service‑account key

# 2️⃣  Build the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "$(gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter="displayName:default" --format="value(email)")",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "serial-port-enable", "value": "TRUE" }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "description": "Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with RTX A6000 GPU"
}
EOF

# 3️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Notes on the JSON body

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type (`n1-standard-8` in this example) |
| `guestAccelerators` | Adds the GPU; `acceleratorType` must be the full URL to the GPU type (`nvidia-a6000`) |
| `disks[0].initializeParams.sourceImage` | Uses the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family |
| `serviceAccounts[0].scopes` | Grants the VM the Cloud‑Platform scope (required for GPU driver installation) |
| `metadata.items` | Enables the serial console (useful for debugging) |
| `tags.items` | Opens ports 80/443 if you plan to run a web server |

---

## Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Billing enabled** – GPU instances require an active billing account.  
2. **GPU quota** – Verify that the zone you choose has available RTX A6000 GPUs (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=$ZONE`).  
3. **API enabled** – Make sure the Compute Engine API is enabled in your project (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
4. **Permissions** – The account you use must have `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (or equivalent) and `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` if you’re attaching a service account.  
5. **Driver installation** – After the VM boots, install the NVIDIA drivers (Google provides a script: `sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall` or use the GPU driver installer from NVIDIA).  

---

### Example Output (gcloud)

```bash
Created [https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances/rtx-a6000-ubuntu].
```

### Example Response (REST)

```json
{
  "id": "1234567890123456789",
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "status": "PROVISIONING",
  ...
}
```

Once the status changes to `RUNNING`, your VM is ready to use. You can SSH into it with:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=$ZONE
```

Happy GPU computing!
